name: Agent-authored skills: create, patch, edit, delete, add/remove supporting files
hermes: `skill_manage` is the agent's procedural memory: actions `create|patch|delete|write_file|remove_file` (plus an undocumented full-rewrite `edit`), an `operations[]` array applied atomically up to 20 ops with per-skill rollback on any failure, `absorbed_into` on delete to migrate cron references, a hard `_validate_frontmatter` blocker and a soft linter, cross-profile 'this skill exists in profile X' error recovery, and cache invalidation + usage telemetry + a debounced sync push after every write. Entries skills-core.tool-skill-manage, .skill-manage-batch, .cross-profile-lookup.
governance: Privileged. A skill write changes what can execute in-process, so create/patch/write_file must keep the existing `skill.generation` contract + CDX-8 quarantine, and delete/activate must cross `skill.install` (`agents/core/kernel/registry.py:106`). Note the honest gap this row inherits: `skill.generation` is a ContractTemplate only and is NOT in `ACTION_REGISTRY`, so today the most privileged skill action — promoting LLM-authored code to executable at `/home/user/jarvis-hub/agents/core/skills/loader.py:979 approve_generated_skill` — is admin_guard'd but never reaches the kernel front door. Register it before widening the write surface.
rationale: Nerva can create a skill and (via a nightly loop) patch one, but cannot refine one inside a session, cannot add a `references/` file, and cannot retire one. Hermes' own finding is that `patch` is the token-cheap action that makes skills actually improve with use; Nerva's create-only path plus a once-a-night proposal cycle is a slow loop with no cheap increments. Extend `generate_skill` into a governed skill-write API with patch/delete/write_file and an atomic batch — reusing the existing quarantine + proposal machinery rather than a second write path.
remaining: - Deleting a skill does not migrate references to it: other skills that name the deleted one are left as they are, and a delete cannot share a batch with the edits that would update them (agents/core/skills/batch.py:214-215).
summary_head: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (ff8641a7), rewritten on the batch-2 re-read: the model has three skill tools, skills_list, skill_view and skill_propose (agents/core/skills/tools.py:86-88, registered at agents/core/skills/tools.py:1130-1139). skill_propose proposes a full new SKILL.md for an existing skill ({name, content}), a new skill from steps ({description, steps}), or, since H665, an ordered batch of Hermes skill_manage operations ({operations}): create, patch (old_string/new_string with replace_all, or whole content, on SKILL.md or any file), write_file and remove_file under references/, templates/, scripts/ or assets/, and delete, which must be the batch's only operation (PROPOSE_SCHEMA, agents/core/skills/tools.py:156-182; PROPOSE_DESCRIPTION, agents/core/skills/tools.py:194-204; ALLOWED_SUBDIRS, agents/core/skills/batch.py:54; agents/core/skills/batch.py:214-215; _apply_op, agents/core/skills/batch.py:423). A proposed batch is dry-run against staging copies first (_propose_batch, agents/core/skills/tools.py:1042; agents/core/skills/tools.py:1077); a failing operation comes back with failed_op, hints and a file_preview, and a passing one is recorded in SkillBatchStore with one approval card (agents/core/skills/tools.py:1111). Only the owner's decision on that card applies it (agents/core/routers/actions.py:147; SkillBatchStore.decide, agents/core/skills/batch.py:889), against the tree fingerprints it was checked on. run_batch (agents/core/skills/batch.py:693) applies eve

name: Skills index in the prompt, cached and prunable under compaction
hermes: build_skills_system_prompt() renders every visible skill as name + one-line description grouped by category, behind a two-layer cache (a lock-protected in-process LRU keyed by tools/toolsets/platform/disabled-set, plus an on-disk snapshot validated against an mtime_ns/size manifest of every SKILL.md). Precedence tiers project > profile/org > external dirs, name-collision flagging, per-skill frontmatter conditions (session_platforms, requires_tools, fallback_for_toolsets), category demotion to names-only under a coding posture. At compaction, loaded skill bodies are replaced by [SKILL_PRUNED: …] markers with a reload notice and a prompt rule that forbids acting on a pruned body. Entries: agent-core-a.skills-index, .skills-cache-clear, .skills-guidance, .skill-pruned-markers, .pruned-skill-reload-notice, .skill-nudge-interval.
governance: read-only. Skill *installation* already crosses the kernel (skill.install, agents/core/kernel/registry.py:96) with a permanent owner floor — that stays untouched.
rationale: The governance half is already better than Hermes'; the presentation half is a flat list rebuilt every turn. Adding the mtime-manifest cache and the [SKILL_PRUNED] contract is what lets a long session load skill bodies at all without the compaction pass silently deleting instructions the model is still following.
remaining: At compaction, loaded skill bodies are not replaced by [SKILL_PRUNED] markers. There is no reload notice and no prompt rule against acting on a pruned body: compaction only makes the dedup forget, so the next skill_view serves the body whole again. The index is not demoted to names only under a coding posture.
summary_head:
Catalogul mărginit de skilluri este injectat în prompt.

The orchestrator puts this index into the agent prompt (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4401-4416). skill_view answers `already_loaded` with a pointer when the session already holds the body, either earlier in this tool loop or carried from an earlier turn by LoadedSkillLedger (agents/core/skills/tools.py:390, agents/core/skills/tools.py:881-890). A compaction makes the loop forget what it served (agents/core/skills/tools.py:342). The L0/L1/L2 ladder (skills_list, skill_view, skill_view with a file) already existed since H318. name: Per-command access tiers (admin vs user, DM vs group scope) and `/whoami`
hermes: `gateway/slash_access.py` splits users already allowed to talk to the bot into admins (every command) and users (only names in `user_allowed_commands`, plus a hard floor of `/help` and `/whoami`), keyed separately for DM and group scope. Denial reads `⛔ /<cmd> is admin-only here. You can run: …`. Re-checked on the cold path, the busy path and again for quick commands. `/whoami` reports platform, scope, user id, tier and the exact command list. Entries gw-slash.access-control / whoami, gw-core.slash-access.
governance: Read-only gate, but it decides who may reach privileged handlers. It sits in front of the kernel, never instead of it — an admin-tier command that acts still crosses its kernel kind.
rationale: Nerva already has the two-tier idea and a snapshot test that keeps it honest; the missing half is projecting it onto chat. Copy the model, invert the default: Hermes fails OPEN (`enabled = bool(admin_ids)`, so no admin list means everyone runs everything, for backward compatibility). Nerva has no back-compat debt here and sells fail-closed, so an unconfigured install must expose only the read-only floor. Also take the improvement Hermes's own rebuild note asks for and it never shipped: audit-log every command denial.
remaining: Tiers are only USER vs ADMIN by principal.admin: there is no per-user allowlist of user-tier commands (Hermes `user_allowed_commands`) and no separate DM vs group scope keying. There is no `/whoami` reporting platform, scope, sender id, tier and the exact command list. A denial is answered and emitted as a `command.completed` extension event with status refused, but it is not written to the audit log.

name: Per-agent persona (SOUL) editing
hermes: A SOUL.md editor in the Profiles panel — a textarea with save (18 profiles-soul-editor), alongside create/rename/delete profile dialogs.
governance: read-only preview; the save is admin_guard'd and versioned, which is the audit trail
rationale: Nerva's persona editing is a versioned, diffed, previewable, rollback-able store; Hermes's is a textarea. An agent's persona is the thing most likely to be edited badly at 2am, and being able to see what changed and go back is worth more than any chrome in this cluster. Nothing to take here.
remaining:
- A persisted create-agent route (from a template or blank) and a HUD dialog
- Rename an agent persistently (not the in-memory override)
- Delete/retire an agent with a confirm dialog
- Tests for create/rename/delete

name: Look back at what the assistant has learned over time
hermes: `hermes journey` (aliases `learning`, `memory-graph`) prints a learning timeline, with list / delete / edit of individual nodes in $EDITOR (05-cli-e.md, 5 entries cli-e.journey*).
governance: read-only; edits to learned material are memory writes and inherit kg.write
rationale: Same capability, richer implementation (a cognitive ledger and reflection lessons rather than a node list). No port.
remaining: The learning timeline feed (GET /api/dashboard/today) still has no per-entry ids, delete or edit, and there is no journey/learning/memory-graph CLI verb; the new GET /api/kg/map and the timeline-aware entity delete cover the graph side only.
